text:
Lina: heads up, bringing up nebula20b-int4 on canary (route=nebula-canary). hitting intermittent OOMs and weird memory fragmentation when concurrent chats hit long tails (users hitting >800 tokens).

Owen: :eyes: can you paste the run command + model config?

Lina: running with our standard int4 profile:
```
model: nebula20b-int4
quant: int4
max_new_tokens: 1024
batching:
  continuous: true
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  max_batch_size: 12
prefetch_kv: true
kv_cache_trim: auto
```
Logs: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.1 GiB (GPU 0; 40.0 GiB total capacity; 34.7 GiB already allocated; 1.8 GiB free; 36.4 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)`

Maya: hmm, that looks like the default max_new_tokens is too high for int4 on 40GB V100-ish instance. We've seen fragmentation when lots of small requests keep creating KV entries.

Sam: also check our prefetched KV growth. If prefetch_kv=true + continuous batching, the per-request KV gets preserved and memory isn't reclaimed until the session ends. That plus 1k new tokens per request will blow the allocator.

Lina: tried toggling `kv_cache_trim: aggressive` in one canary and the OOMs dropped, but latency regressed a touch on tail requests.

Owen: can you share the quick perf numbers?

Lina: before: 95p latency 210ms, after enabling aggressive trim: 95p 260ms, OOMs from ~6/day -> 0.

Maya: tradeoff makes sense. We should try a multi-pronged fix: reduce default `max_new_tokens` for nebula-to 512, add a model-specific batching cap, and schedule periodic KV-trim for long-running conversations rather than immediate aggressive trimming (to avoid extra re-prefetch).

Sam: proposed config (canary) I pushed to infra:
```
model_config:
  nebula20b-int4:
    defaults:
      max_new_tokens: 512
      continuous_batching: true
      max_batch_tokens: 3072
      max_batch_size: 8
    kv_policy:
      prefetch: true
      trim_after_sec: 60
      eviction_policy: lru_by_session_size
```

Owen: also add a per-route override in the router so small short-chat product traffic can still request 1024 if they opt in (route param), but default for general traffic is 512.

Lina: started the canary with that config ~10:30 UTC. Early signs: memory headroom improved, no OOMs after ~20k tokens served.

ci-bot: deploy status: nebula-canary config v12 -> success. 3 instances, rolling restart complete.

Maya: can we also run a quick synthetic workload with many small concurrent sessions to stress fragmentation? I can run a job that simulates 200 concurrent chats with 2-10 messages each and tail lengths randomized 50-900 tokens.

Sam: yes, please. Add instrumentation to record highest allocated memory per-GPU per-session. We want to see peak and churn.

Lina: synthetic run started. initial result: peak per-GPU alloc dropped from 36.4 GiB -> 31.2 GiB and fragmentation metric (free blocks count) reduced by ~30%. No OOMs in 1hr run.

Maya: great. Next steps:
- make `max_new_tokens: 512` the default for nebula20b-int4 in model catalog
- router override for opt-in routes
- add `kv_cache_trim` schedule and LRU eviction by session size
- monitor rollout for 48h, keep canary at 3 instances and scale to 6 if we see sustained lower latencies

Owen: I'll file a quick RFC for the change and link perf dashboards + synthetic test results. Lina, can you capture the failing OOM stack + the successful run logs and drop into the RFC?

Lina: will do, uploading logs now. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
